comment: small->little is a same-register synonym; clean.
wires->cables is a same-register synonym; clean.
'adhesive' is a formal/clinical register shift for a young-teen DIY text vs the casual 'glue'.
much->far preserves meaning and register; clean.
certain->specific is a same-register synonym; clean.
series->sequence is a same-register synonym; clean.
missing indefinite article before 'basic example'.
'for' vs 'about' shifts topic-marking to purpose-marking; still recoverable.
past tense breaks the present-tense instructional frame of the passage.
is->are agreement slip, same pattern as en_seed_04.
third->fourth introduces a factual inconsistency (only three motors are described).
'pick at' (nibble/fidget) is a different phrasal verb from 'pick up' (lift).

errors.learner_form: move him to a new spot
errors.corrected_form: move them to a new spot

comment: 'him' mismatches the plural antecedent 'small things', same pattern as en_seed_10.

errors.corrected_form: tells the motors when to move

comment: dropped 'when' loses the timing content of the instruction.
inserted 'also' plus a shift from direct address (you) to generic 'everyone'.
spelling slip, intended word is clear from context.

errors.learner_form: It says the motors when to move
errors.corrected_form: It tells the motors when to move

comment: 'says' does not take this object+when-clause pattern; reads as a stumble, not just a synonym swap.

errors.learner_form: another motor you can tell to move
errors.corrected_form: you can tell another motor to move

comment: OSV-style reordering, same pattern as en_seed_08; reads as assembled rather than spoken.
dialectal 'y'all' is a formality/register shift against the neutral instructional tone.
inserted negation inverts the claim (can -> cannot).

errors.learner_form: Another motor can't make it move
errors.corrected_form: Another motor can make it move

comment: inserted negation inverts the claim about the motor's function.

errors.learner_form: move them from a new spot
errors.corrected_form: move them to a new spot

comment: to->from reverses source/destination of the movement.
many->few reverses the claim about the Arduino's versatility.

errors.learner_form: The Arduino writes instructions for you
errors.corrected_form: You write instructions for the Arduino

comment: subject/object swap reverses who is doing the writing for whom.
later->first reverses the intended learning progression (simple then complex).
90->9 changes the numeric value by an order of magnitude; not misleading to the reader on its own but a large fidelity departure.
use->avoid inverts the recommendation.
'servo engines' is not the standard term (and is inconsistent with 'motors' used one sentence later).

errors.learner_form: But you can tell another motor
errors.corrected_form: Then you can tell another motor

comment: 'But' signals contrast where the sequence is additive, same pattern as en_seed_12.

errors.learner_form: Also, you need an Arduino board
errors.corrected_form: First, you need an Arduino board

comment: 'Also' loses the sequencing cue that 'First' provides.
specific term 'gripper' flattened to generic 'thing'.
specific term 'commands' flattened to generic 'stuff'.

errors.learner_form: You learned how to connect wires
errors.corrected_form: You learn how to connect wires

comment: four stacked grammar errors across the passage; each is individually recoverable but the density reads rough.

errors.learner_form: another motor you can tell to move
errors.corrected_form: you can tell another motor to move

comment: the inserted slang tag 'yo' plus the OSV reordering make this read assembled rather than spoken.
important->expensive substitutes an unrelated, misleading claim.
